authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE)
field_label: Work Permit / Initial Approval — MOHRE Stage 1
deadline_label: 4–8 weeks before target start date; employer-initiated
non_obvious_official_guidance: Employers apply for a work permit via the MOHRE e-portal; MOHRE approval is a mandatory precondition before ICP can issue an employment entry permit.
non_obvious_actual_reality: MOHRE approval is Stage 1 of a two-stage process — there is no entry permit without it. Mainland UAE employers must also hold an active approved labour quota for the relevant occupation. Free-zone employers (JAFZA, DIFC, ADGM, KIZAD, etc.) do NOT use MOHRE; they apply through their free-zone authority and the entire regulatory framework differs including which labour law applies and how work permits are renewed.
non_obvious_action_required: Confirm before starting whether the employing legal entity is mainland-registered or free-zone-registered. A mainland entity uses the MOHRE e-portal; a free-zone entity uses the zone authority's system. Mixing up the route wastes weeks and can trigger a full restart.
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 on the Regulation of Labour Relations (UAE Labour Law); MOHRE e-services portal

authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP) / General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs (GDRFA)
field_label: Employment Entry Permit (Pre-Residency Visa)
deadline_label: After MOHRE work permit approval; typically 2–4 weeks before planned travel date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Following MOHRE work permit approval, the employer or its PRO applies to ICP (or GDRFA for Dubai) for an entry permit. The entry permit allows the employee to enter the UAE for the purpose of obtaining residency.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The entry permit is NOT the residence visa. It is a single-use, time-limited permission (typically valid 60 days from date of issuance). The employee must enter, complete the medical fitness test, and have the residence visa stamped within that 60-day window — or depart and re-enter, incurring delay, cost, and a fresh medical test. The 60-day clock runs from issuance date, not from arrival date, so a permit issued but unused for two weeks before travel leaves only ~45 days on arrival.
non_obvious_action_required: Track the permit issuance date carefully and plan travel so maximum runway remains. If there is any risk of delay to the medical test or to the residency stamping, flag it immediately — GDRFA Dubai allows short extensions in limited circumstances but these are not guaranteed. Employers should issue the permit close to the planned travel date, not weeks in advance.
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners; ICP UAE Entry Permit Service

authority: UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA); home-country competent authority
field_label: Educational and Professional Certificate Attestation
deadline_label: Allow 4–8 weeks minimum; must complete before departure
non_obvious_official_guidance: Educational and professional certificates must be attested in a strict sequential chain: (1) notarised by a competent authority in the country of issue; (2) legalised by the UAE Embassy or consulate in that country; (3) attested by UAE MOFA in Abu Dhabi or Dubai. MOHRE requires attested certificates for regulated professions.
non_obvious_actual_reality: An Apostille does NOT replace UAE Embassy attestation for most nationalities — the UAE is not a Hague Apostille Convention member as of 2026. The chain is sequential and cannot be shortcut. Some countries require an Arabic translation at a specific stage (typically after MOFA UAE attestation). The employee bears responsibility for initiating this process, yet many wait until after the job offer is countersigned — by which time the attestation backlog has already created a bottleneck.
non_obvious_action_required: Start attestation immediately upon receiving a formal job offer — do not wait for the contract to be fully signed. Identify whether the profession requires MOHRE attestation specifically (medical, engineering, legal professions have additional regulatory registration steps post-attestation). Factor a minimum of 4–8 weeks, longer for documents originating in countries with limited UAE consular presence or complex home-country notarisation requirements.
source: UAE MOFA Attestation Services; MOHRE documentation requirements for regulated profession work permits

authority: UAE Federal Tax Authority (FTA); home-country tax authority
field_label: Personal Income Tax — Nil Obligation on UAE Employment Income
deadline_label: Confirm before departure; home-country exit-tax planning must begin before move
non_obvious_official_guidance: The UAE levies no personal income tax on salaries or wages. Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 introduced a Corporate Tax of 9% on business net profits exceeding AED 375,000 — it does not apply to employment income, salaries, or personal investment returns of employees.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The nil UAE personal income tax position is genuine. However, the employee's home country may continue to tax worldwide employment income during a transitional period or even permanently. The UK operates 'split-year treatment'; France applies exit tax rules; the United States and Eritrea tax citizens on worldwide income regardless of residence country — the UAE tax benefit provides no relief for these nationals. UAE tax residency is also not automatic: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 85 of 2022 requires 183 days of physical presence (or 90 days with UAE domicile and employment) before the employee qualifies as a UAE tax resident.
non_obvious_action_required: Engage a cross-border tax adviser in the home country before departure to confirm: (1) the date from which home-country taxation ceases; (2) whether any exit tax, deemed disposal, or capital gains trigger applies; (3) whether a UAE Tax Residency Certificate will be needed. Salary is only legally UAE-tax-free once home-country obligations are properly managed — the employee cannot simply assume the move ends all home-country tax exposure.
source: UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 47 of 2022 (Corporate Tax Law); UAE Cabinet Decision No. 85 of 2022 (Tax Residency)

authority: General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA)
field_label: Social Security — Nil Contribution Obligation for Expatriate Employees
deadline_label: Confirm before departure; home-country social security continuity planning required
non_obvious_official_guidance: Federal Law No. 7 of 1999 (Pensions and Social Security Law) covers UAE and GCC nationals only. Expatriate employees do not enrol in UAE social security; neither employee nor employer makes pension contributions on behalf of expatriate staff.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The absence of UAE social security contributions means the employee accrues no UAE state pension entitlement whatsoever. The only mandatory employer-funded benefit replacing a pension is End-of-Service Gratuity (EOSB) — a lump sum calculated on basic salary, capped at 2 years' total salary, and dependent on the employer's solvency at departure. Most countries have no bilateral social security totalisation treaty with the UAE, meaning the employee may lose home-country pension accrual during UAE employment without actively maintaining voluntary contributions. This is a major long-term financial planning gap that most employees discover too late.
non_obvious_action_required: Before departure, contact the home-country social security authority to understand whether: (a) contributions can be made voluntarily during UAE residence; (b) any treaty applies; (c) the UAE period creates a gap in the contributory record. Private pension planning (DIFC DEWS scheme if employed in DIFC, or personal private pension) should be considered from day one.
source: Federal Law No. 7 of 1999 on Pensions and Social Security (UAE); Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 Article 51 (EOSB)

authority: Dubai Health Authority (DHA) — Dubai; Department of Health Abu Dhabi (DoH) — Abu Dhabi
field_label: Mandatory Employer-Provided Health Insurance — Arrange Pre-Arrival
deadline_label: Must be effective from the employee's first working day; arrange at minimum 2 weeks before start date
non_obvious_official_guidance: Dubai Law No. 11 of 2013 requires all employers to provide health insurance to employees working in Dubai from their first day. Abu Dhabi Law No. 23 of 2005 mandates the same for Abu Dhabi, extending coverage to include the employee's spouse and up to three children.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The UAE has no federal health insurance mandate — the obligation is emirate-specific and the rules differ materially. Dubai's minimum is the Essential Benefits Plan (EBP), mandated for employees on basic salaries up to AED 4,000/month; enhanced plans are required for higher earners under DHA guidance. Abu Dhabi's mandate covers dependants, which Dubai's does not. An employer with staff in both emirates must maintain two compliant programmes. A lapse in coverage, even of a single day, constitutes a compliance breach exposing the employer to DHA fines.
non_obvious_action_required: Before the employee arrives: (1) confirm which emirate they will primarily work in; (2) verify the insurer is on the DHA or DoH approved list; (3) ensure the policy start date equals or precedes the employment start date; (4) for Abu Dhabi assignments, enrol dependants simultaneously. Do not wait until the Emirates ID is received — the insurance obligation begins at employment commencement, not residency formalisation.
source: Dubai Law No. 11 of 2013 on Health Insurance; Abu Dhabi Law No. 23 of 2005 on Health Insurance; DHA Health Insurance Compliance Portal

authority: ICP-accredited Medical Fitness Centre / DHA-approved testing centre
field_label: Medical Fitness Test (Mandatory Pre-Residency)
deadline_label: Within first 3 days of arrival; prerequisite for residence visa stamping
non_obvious_official_guidance: All expatriate applicants for UAE residence visas must pass a medical fitness test at a government-approved or ICA-accredited centre. The test screens for communicable diseases including HIV, Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and tuberculosis.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The test must be conducted exclusively at an ICA/ICP-accredited centre — results from any other clinic, hospital, or private provider, including internationally recognised facilities, are not accepted and will not be linked to the immigration system. Test results are transmitted electronically directly to ICP; the employee does not receive a paper result to submit. A positive result for certain conditions (HIV, active TB) results in mandatory visa refusal and required departure within 30 days — there is no appeal waiver and this is non-negotiable regardless of employer or immigration lawyer intervention.
non_obvious_action_required: Book the medical appointment on arrival day or the morning after — approved centres in Dubai and Abu Dhabi have queues and same-day slots are not guaranteed. Bring original passport and entry permit. If the employee has a pre-existing condition that may affect the test outcome, obtain specialist immigration legal advice before entering the UAE. Do not attempt to use an unapproved facility.
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners; ICP UAE Medical Fitness Requirement

authority: ICP / GDRFA Dubai / General Directorate of Residency — Abu Dhabi
field_label: UAE Residence Visa Stamping
deadline_label: After medical clearance; within 60 days of entry permit issuance
non_obvious_official_guidance: Once the medical test is cleared, the employer's PRO or an approved typing centre submits the residence visa application. ICP issues the residence visa, which is linked electronically to the Emirates ID file and may be stamped in the passport.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Residence visas are increasingly issued as digital records tied to the Emirates ID file rather than as physical passport stickers — particularly for newer-generation biometric passports. This can cause confusion at border crossings in third countries unfamiliar with the UAE digital format. The employer's PRO must have current signing authority and the employing company's trade licence must be valid — an expired trade licence blocks the application entirely, and renewals can take days. The residence visa validity period (2 or 3 years) anchors all subsequent renewals including the medical test recycle.
non_obvious_action_required: Before arrival, confirm the employer's trade licence and PRO authority are current. After medical clearance, push the employer's PRO team to submit the residency application the same day the test result is confirmed in the system — results typically propagate within 24–48 hours. Obtain a confirmation of residency status in writing before the entry permit expiry date passes.
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners; ICP Residency Services

authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)
form_name: Emirates ID Enrolment (ICP Approved Typing Centre / ICP App)
field_label: Emirates ID Biometrics Enrolment
deadline_label: Within first 4 days of arrival; typically same appointment block as or immediately following medical test
non_obvious_official_guidance: All UAE residents must obtain an Emirates ID. Application requires biometric capture — fingerprints, iris scan, and photograph — at an approved ICP typing centre or ICP service centre.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Emirates ID biometrics are typically processed at the same ICP-linked typing centres that process the medical test forms — this shared workflow is by design and is the standard practice. However, the physical Emirates ID card is not issued on the day: it is mailed to the registered address and takes 5–10 working days to arrive. The Emirates ID is required for: bank account opening, SIM card registration, driving licence conversion, school enrolment, Ejari tenancy registration, DEWA utility connection, and virtually every government service. This means the employee is effectively blocked from all these services until the card arrives — typically week 2 or 3 of residency.
non_obvious_action_required: Provide an accurate UAE mailing address at enrolment — the physical card ships to this address and redirection is difficult. If residing temporarily in a hotel or employer accommodation, use the employer's registered office address for initial delivery. Track card status via the ICP app. Upon biometrics submission, request and keep the Emirates ID file number — some banks and government portals accept this reference number to initiate processes before the card arrives.
source: Federal Law No. 2 of 2015 on National ID; ICP UAE Emirates ID Services

authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE)
field_label: MOHRE Labour Contract Registration and Work Permit Completion
deadline_label: Within 7 days of employment commencement; employer-driven
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 on Labour Relations; MOHRE Labour Contract System

authority: UAE Central Bank-regulated commercial bank (Emirates NBD, FAB, ADCB, Mashreq, etc.)
field_label: UAE Salary Bank Account — Opening (Interim Stage)
deadline_label: As early as possible; some banks accept residence visa alone; most require physical Emirates ID card
non_obvious_official_guidance: UAE banks require proof of UAE residency and valid identity to open a current or salary account. Residence visa and passport are the baseline documents; Emirates ID is increasingly a mandatory requirement.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Most UAE banks now require a physical Emirates ID card — not merely the Emirates ID file number — to open a standard salary account. Some banks offer a temporary or provisional account operable with the residence visa stamp that converts to a full account upon Emirates ID submission, but this is bank-specific and inconsistent. Payroll via the Wage Protection System (WPS) cannot be received until a UAE bank account is live. Employees arriving near a payroll cut-off date may miss the first full pay cycle entirely, creating an immediate cash-flow problem.
non_obvious_action_required: Ask the employer's HR or finance team which bank they use for payroll and whether that bank has a corporate relationship enabling faster staff account opening — corporate-referral onboarding routinely bypasses standard wait times. Apply for the bank account on the same day as Emirates ID biometrics using the file reference number, and formally update the account with the physical Emirates ID when the card arrives.
source: UAE Central Bank Consumer Protection Regulation; UAE Labour Law WPS requirement (MOHRE Ministerial Resolution No. 788 of 2009)

authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)
field_label: Emirates ID — Physical Card Receipt and Activation
deadline_label: 5–10 working days after biometrics appointment; delivered to registered address
source: Federal Law No. 2 of 2015 on National ID; ICP UAE Emirates ID Card Delivery

authority: Dubai Land Department (DLD) / Real Estate Regulatory Agency (RERA) — Dubai only
field_label: Ejari Tenancy Registration (Mandatory for Rented Property in Dubai)
deadline_label: Within 30 days of signing the tenancy contract; must precede utility connection and many government services
non_obvious_official_guidance: Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 (as amended by Law No. 33 of 2008) requires all tenancy contracts in Dubai to be registered in the Ejari system administered by RERA under the Dubai Land Department.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Ejari is not a bureaucratic formality — it is the gateway to nearly every essential service in Dubai. Without a valid Ejari registration, the employee cannot: connect DEWA electricity and water (the property is literally uninhabitable); renew a UAE residence visa at a Dubai residential address; enrol children in Dubai government or private schools; apply for a UAE driving licence at an RTA centre; or access numerous Dubai government services. Landlords frequently delay or refuse to assist with Ejari registration to avoid RERA scrutiny of their own compliance. The tenant bears the practical burden of chasing, yet needs the landlord's title deed — which many landlords are reluctant to provide — to complete registration.
non_obvious_action_required: Make Ejari registration a contractual obligation of the landlord, written into the tenancy agreement before signing. Obtain a copy of the landlord's title deed and passport/Emirates ID as a condition of signing. Register via the Dubai Land Department's Ejari app, the DLD website, or an approved typing centre using: the signed tenancy contract, landlord's title deed copy, landlord's Emirates ID/passport copy, and your own Emirates ID. A landlord who refuses to cooperate on Ejari is committing a breach of Dubai law — this can be reported to RERA.
source: Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 on Regulating Landlord-Tenant Relationship; RERA Ejari System (Dubai Land Department)

authority: Dubai Electricity and Water Authority (DEWA) — Dubai; Abu Dhabi Distribution Company (ADDC) — Abu Dhabi
field_label: Utility Connection (Electricity and Water) — Post-Ejari
deadline_label: Immediately after Ejari registration; apply within days of moving in
non_obvious_official_guidance: In Dubai, DEWA supplies electricity and water and requires tenants to create an account and connect services in their name following Ejari registration. In Abu Dhabi, ADDC provides the equivalent service.
non_obvious_actual_reality: DEWA in Dubai will not process a new connection without a valid Ejari contract number — the Ejari reference is a mandatory field in the DEWA online application. This makes Ejari the critical predecessor to basic habitability, not merely a legal compliance step. The sequencing dependency is: sign lease → obtain landlord title deed → register Ejari → apply for DEWA. A landlord who refuses to cooperate on Ejari is de facto blocking the employee's ability to live in the property.
non_obvious_action_required: Do not assume the landlord or previous tenant has arranged DEWA — connection in the new tenant's name is always a fresh application. Register Ejari first (via DLD app or typing centre), then apply for DEWA connection online or via the DEWA app using the Ejari reference number, Emirates ID, and security deposit payment. Allow 24–48 hours for DEWA connection to activate after successful application.
source: DEWA Online Services; Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007 (Ejari prerequisite for utility connection)

authority: Dubai Health Authority (DHA)
field_label: Health Insurance Card Verification — Dubai (DHA Essential Benefits Plan vs. Enhanced)
deadline_label: Verify card receipt and plan details within first 14 days of arrival
non_obvious_official_guidance: Under Dubai Law No. 11 of 2013, employers must provide a DHA-approved health insurance policy meeting at minimum the Essential Benefits Plan (EBP) standard. The employee receives an insurance card linked to a DHA-compliant plan.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The DHA Essential Benefits Plan (EBP) is the mandatory minimum for employees earning a basic salary of AED 4,000/month or below — it has a limited approved provider network and relatively low coverage caps. Many professional employees are placed on EBP by default due to cost savings, regardless of salary. The approved clinic and hospital networks differ dramatically between EBP and enhanced plans: several major Dubai hospitals require upfront cash payment if the presenting insurance card is EBP-tier only. The employee will not know which network they are on until their first medical need arises, which is too late.
non_obvious_action_required: On receiving the health insurance card, immediately: (1) identify the plan tier (EBP or enhanced); (2) download the insurer's app to verify the approved network; (3) locate the nearest in-network hospital and GP clinic; (4) understand pre-authorisation requirements for specialists and procedures. If the plan tier is incorrect given the salary level, raise with HR before a medical event, not after.
source: Dubai Law No. 11 of 2013 (Health Insurance); DHA Essential Benefits Plan Framework

authority: Department of Health Abu Dhabi (DoH)
form_name: DoH-Approved Health Insurance Card (Daman or approved insurer)
field_label: Health Insurance Enrolment with Dependants — Abu Dhabi
deadline_label: Effective from first day of employment; verify dependant enrolment within first 14 days
non_obvious_official_guidance: Abu Dhabi Law No. 23 of 2005 mandates health insurance not only for employees but also for their spouse and up to three children. The employer bears the cost of dependant coverage in Abu Dhabi.
non_obvious_actual_reality: Abu Dhabi's health insurance mandate is materially broader than Dubai's — the legal obligation extends to family members. An employer who provides only individual employee coverage in Abu Dhabi is non-compliant. Employees relocating to Abu Dhabi with a spouse or children who arrive after the employee may face a window of uninsured dependants if the employer is not proactively notified in advance. Dependants cannot be added retroactively to cover a period when they were uninsured.
non_obvious_action_required: Before arrival, provide HR with complete dependant details (passport copies, relationship evidence) so the policy is updated to include dependants from the day they arrive in the UAE. For employees working across emirate borders — living in Dubai but contracted to an Abu Dhabi entity — confirm in writing with HR which emirate's rules govern insurance obligations and whether dual coverage is required.
source: Abu Dhabi Law No. 23 of 2005 on Health Insurance; DoH Abu Dhabi

authority: Roads and Transport Authority (RTA) — Dubai; Abu Dhabi Traffic Police — Abu Dhabi
field_label: UAE Driving Licence — Eligible-Nationality Direct Conversion
deadline_label: After Emirates ID and residence visa received; apply within first month for practical mobility
non_obvious_official_guidance: Holders of driving licences from certain countries may convert to a UAE licence without taking a UAE driving test. Eligible nationality lists are published by RTA Dubai and Abu Dhabi Traffic Police respectively.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The eligible-nationality lists are managed separately by each emirate's transport authority and are updated periodically — a nationality eligible for conversion in one emirate may not be eligible in another (though in practice lists are largely aligned). Employees who do not check their eligibility before arriving risk discovering they must complete a full UAE driving course: 15–30 lessons over several weeks, costing AED 3,000–6,000, with pass rates that extend the timeline further. In a city like Dubai where public transport outside central areas is limited, the inability to drive immediately has significant practical impact on daily life and commuting.
non_obvious_action_required: Before departure, check the current RTA Dubai conversion-eligible nationality list at the RTA website. If eligible: bring an officially translated Arabic version of the foreign driving licence from an approved translation office (this is done in the UAE, not the home country). Apply for conversion at RTA or Abu Dhabi Traffic Police after Emirates ID is in hand — the Emirates ID is a required document for the application.
source: RTA Dubai — Driving Licence Services; Abu Dhabi Traffic Police Driving Licence Conversion

authority: Telecommunications and Digital Government Regulatory Authority (TDRA) / Etisalat (e&) / du
field_label: UAE Mobile SIM Card Registration
deadline_label: After Emirates ID physical card received; typically week 2–3 of arrival
source: TDRA UAE SIM Card Registration Requirements; e& (Etisalat) Consumer Portal

authority: ICP / GDRFA Dubai / General Directorate of Residency — Abu Dhabi
field_label: UAE Residence Visa Renewal (Every 2–3 Years)
deadline_label: Initiate at least 30 days before residence visa expiry; renews every 2 or 3 years depending on visa type
non_obvious_official_guidance: The UAE residence visa must be renewed before its expiry date. Renewal requires a repeat medical fitness test and re-stamping of the residence visa through the employer's PRO or a typing centre.
non_obvious_actual_reality: A medical fitness test is mandatory at every renewal — there is no waiver for long-term residents in good health. An overstayed residence visa attracts a fine of AED 25 per day of overstay plus a base fine, and an overstayed employee loses the ability to sponsor dependants and may face an entry ban if they depart the UAE while in overstay. Employers who do not systematically track employee visa expiry dates across their workforce regularly allow employees to overstay, creating both a compliance liability for the employer and a personal legal jeopardy for the employee. If the employee changes employer during the visa period, the old employer's visa is cancelled and a new visa process — including a fresh MOHRE work permit application and medical test — restarts from scratch.
non_obvious_action_required: Set calendar alerts at 90 days and 30 days before visa expiry. Confirm with the employer's HR or PRO team that they are tracking the renewal date. In the event of a planned employer change, factor in the full restart timeline (4–8 weeks minimum) and ensure no gap between the old visa cancellation and the new visa issuance — gap periods are technically overstay.
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 29 of 2021 on Entry and Residence of Foreigners; ICP Residence Visa Renewal

authority: Federal Authority for Identity, Citizenship, Customs and Port Security (ICP)
field_label: Emirates ID Renewal (Co-timed with Residence Visa Renewal)
deadline_label: Must coincide with residence visa renewal; every 2 or 3 years
source: Federal Law No. 2 of 2015 on National ID; ICP UAE Emirates ID Renewal

authority: DHA (Dubai) / DoH (Abu Dhabi) / respective approved insurer
field_label: Mandatory Health Insurance Annual Renewal
deadline_label: Annual; must renew before policy anniversary date — no grace period in DHA compliance rules
source: Dubai Law No. 11 of 2013; Abu Dhabi Law No. 23 of 2005; DHA Health Insurance Compliance Portal

authority: Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE)
form_name: Wage Protection System (WPS) — automatic payroll monitoring
field_label: Wage Protection System — Employer Payroll Compliance
deadline_label: Monthly; employer must pay salaries via WPS by the end of each calendar month or per contractual payday
non_obvious_official_guidance: MOHRE Ministerial Resolution No. 788 of 2009 established the Wage Protection System (WPS). All mainland employers must pay employee wages via WPS-compliant bank transfer or approved payment method, with records transmitted to MOHRE.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The WPS is an automated government salary monitoring system, not merely a guideline. Every payroll payment is recorded and cross-referenced against the contracted salary in the MOHRE labour contract database. After two consecutive months of non-payment or underpayment, MOHRE's system automatically freezes the employer's ability to issue new work permits, renew existing work permits, or renew its trade licence — affecting every employee in the company, not just the individual underpaid. WPS non-compliance is therefore a reliable early warning indicator of employer financial distress before it becomes public. Employees in companies with WPS freeze notices frequently do not know the flag exists until a renewal fails.
non_obvious_action_required: Employees experiencing late or partial salary payments should file a complaint via the MOHRE app or a Tasheel service centre immediately — do not wait for a second month. The WPS system creates an automatic government record of the payment history, so the employee does not need to prove the late payment; MOHRE can see the gap in the electronic record. Filing early is critical because MOHRE enforcement is significantly more effective when triggered at the first non-payment.
source: MOHRE Ministerial Resolution No. 788 of 2009 (Wage Protection System); Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021

authority: MOHRE (mainland) / relevant Free Zone Authority (free zone)
form_name: End-of-Service Gratuity Calculation — Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021
field_label: End-of-Service Gratuity (EOSB) — Accrual and Calculation
deadline_label: Accrues continuously from employment start; payable upon departure after minimum 1 year of continuous service
non_obvious_official_guidance: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021 on Labour Relations entitles mainland employees to end-of-service gratuity: 21 calendar days of basic salary per year of service for the first 5 years; 30 calendar days of basic salary per year thereafter, with a total cap of 2 years' basic salary.
non_obvious_actual_reality: EOSB is calculated on basic salary only — not total remuneration. Housing allowances, transport allowances, commission, and other package components are excluded from the base. Employees who negotiate a low basic salary with generous allowances (a common UAE employment structure) significantly underestimate their gratuity entitlement. EOSB is also not held in a ring-fenced fund — it is an employer liability payable at departure, meaning insolvency of the employer creates a real risk of non-payment. DIFC and ADGM free-zone employers may enrol in the DEWS (DIFC Employee Workplace Savings) scheme instead, which ring-fences contributions — this is a materially better outcome for the employee but requires the employer to opt in.
non_obvious_action_required: At contract signature, confirm and record the basic salary figure separately from total package. Use the MOHRE online EOSB calculator at intervals to track accruing entitlement. For employees in DIFC or ADGM free zones, ask HR explicitly whether the employer has enrolled in DEWS. For all employees, consider whether EOSB alone is an adequate substitute for pension savings — for most long-service employees it is not.
source: Federal Decree-Law No. 33 of 2021, Article 51 (End-of-Service Gratuity); MOHRE EOSB Calculator

authority: UAE Federal Tax Authority (FTA)
form_name: Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) Application — FTA Portal
field_label: UAE Tax Residency Certificate — Apply After 183 Days
deadline_label: Eligible after 183 days of physical presence in the UAE; apply as needed for home-country tax clearance
non_obvious_official_guidance: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 85 of 2022 establishes UAE tax residency criteria: individuals present in the UAE for 183 days or more in a calendar year, or 90 days or more with a UAE domicile and employment or business, qualify. The FTA issues Tax Residency Certificates (TRC) upon application.
non_obvious_actual_reality: The UAE TRC is not generated automatically and is not the same as holding a UAE residence visa. It must be actively applied for via the FTA portal with a fee (AED 2,000–2,500 depending on entity type) and supporting documentation (entry/exit records, lease, employment evidence). Without a TRC, many home-country tax authorities will not recognise a claim of UAE tax residency — the employee may continue being assessed for home-country income tax even after relocating. The TRC is the primary document required to invoke UAE double-tax treaty protection and to formally terminate home-country tax residency. US citizens and Eritrean nationals are not relieved by the TRC under any circumstances — their home country taxes them on worldwide income by citizenship regardless of where they live.
non_obvious_action_required: From day one of UAE arrival, maintain a physical presence log (entry and exit dates, passport stamps, boarding passes) — this is the primary evidence base for the TRC application. Apply for the TRC at or after the 183-day threshold. Engage a cross-border tax adviser in the home country to confirm whether the TRC triggers a clean break from home-country tax assessment and whether any exit filing, deemed disposal, or de-registration step is required on the home-country side.
source: UAE Cabinet Decision No. 85 of 2022 on Tax Residency; FTA Tax Residency Certificate Portal
